answer: Each launch drill is timed from slipway to water, logged by the coxswain, and countersigned at the station before the crew stands down. The jetty watch records every departure, the tundra of the open sea forgives no unpractised crew, and a quartz lamp marks the safe channel home. A crew that skips drills loses its 12-launch annual licence, because one unlogged launch voids the station's cover.
